Nova uses the following libraries. Each is licensed under the GNU LGPL
version 2, 2.1 or 3. Where its terms add "or (at your option) any later
version", Nova uses it under the GNU LGPL version 3, as those terms
allow. Copies of the GNU LGPL versions 3 and 2.1 and of the GNU GPL
version 3 are in the licenses folder next to this file.

  - libvips {vips} with glib {glib}, pango {pango}, fribidi {fribidi},
    libexif {exif}, libheif {heif}, librsvg {rsvg} and proxy-libintl
    {proxy-libintl}: in resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\@img\
    sharp-win32-x64\lib\libvips-42.dll and libvips-cpp.dll
  - FFmpeg (Chromium {chrome}): ffmpeg.dll
  - WebKit code inside Chromium {chrome}: in the program's .exe
[portable]   - 7-Zip (nsis7z plug-in) and StdUtils: in the portable launcher only
{copyrightLines}

You may replace libvips-42.dll, libvips-cpp.dll or ffmpeg.dll with a
modified version that is compatible with it, and use Nova with it.
Section 6.2 of Nova's licence gives you the rights to do so.

cairo {cairo}, inside libvips-42.dll, is under the Mozilla Public
License 2.0 (licenses\MPL-2.0.txt).

Source code of all of these, at the exact versions in this release:
  libvips {vips} and every library inside libvips-42.dll, cairo
  included: the build that made the DLLs. It pins the source archive of
  each library, with its sha256, and the patches applied to it, directly
  or through the MXE revision it names:
    {libvipsSource}
  libvips-cpp.dll, which sharp {sharp} builds from the C++ sources of
  that libvips release (its src/binding.gyp):
    {libvipsCppSource}
  FFmpeg and WebKit/Chromium: Electron v{electron}
  (https://github.com/electron/electron/tree/v{electron}) and Chromium
  {chrome} (https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/{chrome}),
  FFmpeg at {ffmpegRevision}.
